#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$root=(Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../..')).ProviderPath
$test=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.Tests.ps1'
$correct=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockCorrect.psm1'
$wrong=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrong.psm1'
$wrongEmpty=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrongEmpty.psm1'
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ReportDirectory,'Run independent planner mock gate and save evidence')){return}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReportDirectory -Force|Out-Null
$runs=@()
foreach($case in @(@{name='correct';module=$correct},@{name='wrong';module=$wrong},@{name='wrong-empty';module=$wrongEmpty})){
    $env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE=$case.module
    $configuration=New-PesterConfiguration
    $configuration.Run.Path=@($test)
    $configuration.Run.PassThru=$true
    $configuration.Output.Verbosity='Detailed'
    $configuration.TestResult.Enabled=$true
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputFormat='NUnitXml'
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputPath=Join-Path $ReportDirectory ($case.name+'.xml')
    $result=Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
    $cases=@($result.Tests | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{name=$_.Name;result=[string]$_.Result} })
    $runs+= [pscustomobject]@{name=$case.name;passed=$result.PassedCount;failed=$result.FailedCount;skipped=$result.SkippedCount;cases=$cases}
}
Remove-Item Env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if($runs[0].passed -ne 6 -or $runs[0].failed -ne 0 -or $runs[0].skipped -ne 0){throw 'Correct mock did not pass every planner case.'}
foreach($case in $runs[0].cases){
    $controls=@($runs[1..2] | ForEach-Object { $_.cases | Where-Object name -CEQ $case.name })
    if($controls.Count -ne 2 -or @($controls | Where-Object result -EQ 'Failed').Count -eq 0){throw "No rejecting negative control for: $($case.name)"}
}
$receipt=[pscustomobject]@{
    timestamp=Get-Date -Format s
    root=$root
    test=(Resolve-Path $test).ProviderPath
    testSha256=(Get-FileHash $test -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    correctMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $correct -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrong -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongEmptyMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrongEmpty -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    runs=$runs
    qualification='Catch-up mock sensitivity check. This receipt does not backdate or replace the original pre-implementation gate.'
}
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6|Set-Content (Join-Path $ReportDirectory 'mock-gate.json')
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Method,
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Name,
    [string]$Id = '',
    [string]$FrId = '',
    [string]$TrId = '',
    [string]$TestId = ''
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

Import-Module powershell-yaml -ErrorAction Stop
$repl = '[HOME]/github/mcpserver-claude-code-plugin/lib/repl-invoke.ps1'
$outDir = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'qbrain-readback'
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $outDir)) { $null = New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $outDir }

$params = [ordered]@{}
if ($Id) { $params['id'] = $Id }
if ($FrId) { $params['frId'] = $FrId }
if ($TrId) { $params['trId'] = $TrId }
if ($TestId) { $params['testId'] = $TestId }
$yaml = if ($params.Count) { ConvertTo-Yaml $params } else { '{}' }

Set-Location -LiteralPath '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs'
$output = & pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File $repl -Method $Method -ParamsYaml $yaml 2>&1
$exit = $LASTEXITCODE
$path = Join-Path $outDir ($Name + '.txt')
$output | Set-Content -LiteralPath $path
[pscustomobject]@{
    method   = $Method
    params   = $params
    exitCode = $exit
    lines    = @($output).Count
    path     = $path
    readAt   = (Get-Date -Format s)
} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$IndexPath = '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs/docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/round4-frozen-evidence-f35b696/evidence-index.json'
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

function Get-JUnitCase {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $cases = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testcase'))
    $failed = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('failure') -or $_.SelectSingleNode('error') }).Count
    $skipped = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('skipped') }).Count
    $names = @($cases | ForEach-Object { '{0} :: {1}' -f $_.GetAttribute('classname'), $_.GetAttribute('name') })
    $suites = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testsuite') | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object)
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Count        = $cases.Count
        Failed       = $failed
        Skipped      = $skipped
        Names        = $names
        FirstSuiteTs = if ($suites.Count) { $suites[0] } else { '' }
        LastSuiteTs  = if ($suites.Count) { $suites[-1] } else { '' }
    }
}

function Get-TrxCase {
    param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $ns = New-Object System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager($doc.NameTable)
    $ns.AddNamespace('t', 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010')
    $results = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $ns))
    $outcomes = $results | Group-Object { $_.GetAttribute('outcome') } | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Count }
    $counters = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary/t:Counters', $ns)
    $times = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:Times', $ns)
    $defs = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTest', $ns))
    $names = @($defs | ForEach-Object {
            $tm = $_.SelectSingleNode('t:TestMethod', $ns)
            '{0} :: {1}' -f $tm.GetAttribute('className'), $tm.GetAttribute('name')
        })
    [pscustomobject]@{
        Count    = $results.Count
        Outcomes = ($outcomes -join ',')
        Counters = if ($counters) { ($counters.Attributes | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Value }) -join ',' } else { '' }
        Times    = if ($times) { ($times.Attributes | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Value }) -join ',' } else { '' }
        Names    = $names
    }
}

$index = Get-Content -LiteralPath $IndexPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
'INDEX revision=' + $index.revision + ' timestamp=' + $index.timestamp
$manifestHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $index.sourceManifest -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
'MANIFEST sha256 match=' + ($manifestHash -eq $index.sourceManifestSha256) + ' actual=' + $manifestHash
foreach ($r in $index.reports) {
    $jh = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $r.junit -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $th = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $r.trx -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $j = Get-JUnitCase -Path $r.junit
    $t = Get-TrxCase -Path $r.trx
    $jSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$j.Names)
    $tSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$t.Names)
    $onlyJ = @($j.Names | Where-Object { -not $tSet.Contains($_) })
    $onlyT = @($t.Names | Where-Object { -not $jSet.Contains($_) })
    $dupJ = @($j.Names | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object Name)
    [pscustomobject]@{
        name           = $r.name
        junitHashMatch = ($jh -eq $r.junitSha256)
        trxHashMatch   = ($th -eq $r.trxSha256)
        indexCases     = $r.cases
        junitCases     = $j.Count
        junitFailed    = $j.Failed
        junitSkipped   = $j.Skipped
        junitFirstTs   = $j.FirstSuiteTs
        junitLastTs    = $j.LastSuiteTs
        trxCases       = $t.Count
        trxOutcomes    = $t.Outcomes
        trxCounters    = $t.Counters
        trxTimes       = $t.Times
        onlyInJUnit    = $onlyJ.Count
        onlyInTrx      = $onlyT.Count
        duplicateNames = $dupJ.Count
        junitWrite     = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $r.junit).LastWriteTime.ToString('s')
        trxWrite       = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $r.trx).LastWriteTime.ToString('s')
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
}

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param()

# Prints only file paths and match counts. Never prints the secret or any part of it.
Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

Import-Module powershell-yaml -ErrorAction Stop
$repo = '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs'
$marker = ConvertFrom-Yaml (Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repo 'AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml') -Raw)
$key = ([string]$marker['apiKey']).Trim()
$prefix = $key.Substring(0, 8)

Set-Location -LiteralPath $repo
$tracked = @(git ls-files -- docs tests scripts src README.md)
$extra = @(
    Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repo 'docs/receipts/hv') -File -Force | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName.Substring($repo.Length + 1) }
    Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repo 'docs/receipts/hv/claude-opus-round4-tools') -File -Recurse -Force | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName.Substring($repo.Length + 1) }
)
$files = @($tracked + $extra | Sort-Object -Unique)
$hits = 0
foreach ($rel in $files) {
    $full = Join-Path $repo $rel
    $item = Get-Item -LiteralPath $full -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $item -or $item.PSIsContainer -or $item.Length -gt 50MB) { continue }
    $text = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($full)
    $fullCount = ([regex]::Matches($text, [regex]::Escape($key))).Count
    $preCount = ([regex]::Matches($text, [regex]::Escape($prefix))).Count
    if ($fullCount -gt 0 -or $preCount -gt 0) {
        $hits++
        '{0} fullKey={1} prefix8={2} tracked={3}' -f $rel, $fullCount, $preCount, ($tracked -contains $rel)
    }
}
'SCANNED={0} FILES-WITH-MATCH={1}' -f $files.Count, $hits

    }

)

}

1	# Guest game and GitHub admin PWA release
2	
3	Current operator scope, 28 October 2026. This document supersedes the public
4	OpenAI sign-in, public PWA installation and browser role-delegation portions of
5	the earlier designs. QBrain is authoritative; this is its linked implementation
6	and verification projection. Implementation and hosted rollout are in progress.
7	
8	## Behavior and boundaries
9	
10	The public game accepts guests only. Generated aliases, icons, browser-persistent
11	guest credentials, rooms, private live updates and reactions remain available.
12	Public OpenAI login/callback routes return404. Public session responses expose no
13	administration permissions, stored/bootstrap grants do not elevate guests, and
14	member-shaped public sessions are rejected. Community suggestion/nomination UI
15	and the former `/content` entry are inactive in this release.
16	
17	Administration uses the registered [Word Pairs Admin GitHub App](https://github.com/settings/apps/word-pairs-admin-sharpninja).
18	Only verified GitHub numeric account16146732 and login `sharpninja` can complete
19	sign-in. The private App requests no repository, organization or email permissions
20	and has no webhook. User-access delegation is disabled: `/admin/users` redirects
21	to `/admin` and its API returns404 without touching access storage. Existing ACL
22	and community policy/domain/history remain preserved for future scope.
23	
24	Server configuration uses `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and
25	`WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, never public-prefixed variables. Both callback
26	URLs are registered exactly:
27	
28	- `https://wordpairs.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (staging).
29	- `https://wordpairs-j9jf.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (production).
30	
31	The provider uses Authorization Code with S256PKCE and state. Existing persisted
32	challenges are browser-bound, expire after10minutes and are consumed before
33	callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
34	retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
35	`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
36	namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
37	reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
38	Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.
39	
40	## Installation and offline behavior
41	
42	Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
43	start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
44	Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
45	The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
46	recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.
47	
48	Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
49	`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
50	and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
51	admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
52	the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
53	mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
54	is queued for later execution.
55	
56	Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
57	`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
58	credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
59	updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.
60	
61	Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
62	as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
63	caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
64	root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
65	code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.
66	
67	## Traceability and repeatable cases
68	
69	QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
70	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
71	`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
72	`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
73	`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
74	`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
75	preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
76	and independent review justify a separate status update.
77	
78	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
79	  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
80	  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
81	  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
82	  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
83	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
84	  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
85	  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
86	  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
87	  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
88	  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
89	  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
90	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
91	  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
92	  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
93	  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
94	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
95	  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
96	  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
97	  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
98	  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
99	  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
100	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
101	 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
102	  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.
103	
104	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
105	administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
106	session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
107	adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
108	Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
109	opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
110	Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
111	matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.
112	
113	Ordered actions and expected observations:
114	
115	1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
116	   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
117	   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
118	2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
119	   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
120	   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
121	3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
122	   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
123	   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
124	4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
125	   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
126	   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
127	5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
128	   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
129	   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.
130	
131	Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
132	contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
133	contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
134	ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
135	not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.
136	
137	The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
138	network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
139	checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
140	The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
141	it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
142	[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).
143	
144	```gherkin
145	Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
146	  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
147	  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
148	  Then no administrator profile is returned
149	  And no private catalog records are read
150	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
151	  Then the callback creates no administrator session
152	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
153	  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
154	  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
155	  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
156	  When the administrator signs out
157	  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
158	  And the guest session remains usable
159	```
160	
161	## Verification, operations and open dependencies
162	
163	Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
164	`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
165	suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
166	and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
167	`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
168	`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. The hostile-review correction adds forward
169	migration `012_guest_public_profiles.sql`; no package is added. Existing schema
170	and private Realtime/scheduler remain separate deployment prerequisites.
171	
172	Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
173	actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
174	the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
175	cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
176	full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
177	`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
178	disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
179	native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
180	TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.
181	
182	The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
183	refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
184	Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
185	browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
186	now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
187	desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.
188	
189	Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
190	OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
191	The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
192	feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
193	Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
194	standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
195	distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
196	name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.
197	
198	## Hostile-review recovery slice
199	
200	Claude Opus round1 rejected candidate437c501 at92%accuracy/88%completeness.
201	Its full findings and persistence proof are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/`.
202	The owner was created with the former member public-default, without a public
203	preferences route. The earlier PostgreSQL public-read failure exposed the extra
204	row; fixture cleanup made the suite independent but did not repair that product
205	privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.
206	
207	The operator confirmed: "Hide all old member profiles". GA-10 therefore requires
208	new members to default private and all member identities, including retired
209	OpenAI records, to be excluded by the server's public query even if their stored
210	flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and
211	revision conflicts. Add a forward SQL migration after the existing hosted history;
212	apply it to staging first, verify, then production. No data deletion or provider
213	token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal
214	five-minute read lifetime; restart/deployment creates fresh application caches.
215	
216	Before this correction, the independent GA-10 oracle accepted a private member
217	and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
218	The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to
219	the real identity service and PostgreSQL query. This is evidence for the recovery
220	slice, not a reconstruction of the missing original pre-implementation gate.
221	The original slice's chronological process receipt remains missing and is not
222	claimed satisfied. On28October2026 the operator explicitly answered "Record the
223	one-time exception" to question `call_30e2a1f3011842979ab422d87f21432e`. This is a
224	one-time exception for that historical missing receipt only. It does not waive
225	fresh hostile validation, current tests, security checks, migration verification
226	or hosted observations. No original chronology is reconstructed. The decision
227	and QBrain readback are retained in `docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/process-exception.json`.
228	All current status/criteria remain in progress/unsatisfied.
229	
230	Recovery work also supplies explicit GA-05/06/07 cross-references to canonical
231	PWA criteria and their TEST/TR records, GA-09 on the responsive TR/admin TEST,
232	reproducible adapter fixtures and full post-edit PWA browser execution. No prior
233	failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable
234	unit, PostgreSQL, browser, lint and production-build checks.
235	
236	Claude Opus round2 rejected the corrective candidate at95%accuracy and
237	94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
238	planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
239	source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
240	adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
241	`docs/receipts/hv/`. Later reviews and dispositions are recorded below.
242	
243	For the next review, a PowerShell schema planner and CLI replace the Node planner.
244	An initial planner module and five-case mock gate preceded the sixth test case;
245	the six-case gate preceded the final module edit, not the initial module. A later
246	catch-up gate added a rejecting negative control for every case. These receipts do
247	not change the original chronology. The mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in
248	`docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/planner-*`. The tracked source-manifest
249	generator enumerates literal Git paths, including bracketed routes, public assets
250	and root test/build configuration; the frozen review manifest records its path count.
251	The adapter analyzer receipt records parser and ScriptAnalyzer results for both
252	scripts before the fresh three-fixture run. These are local process receipts, not
253	approval to deploy. The final source manifest and all execution reports must be
254	regenerated against the frozen source revision that the next hostile review sees.
255	
256	Round3 first ended incomplete during the MCP outage. Its later Claude Opus retry
257	returned DISAGREE at95% accuracy and93% completeness: 31 PASS, four FAIL and three
258	UNKNOWN. Round4 returned DISAGREE at96% accuracy and94% completeness: 35 PASS,
259	five FAIL and three UNKNOWN. The full request, response, findings and protected
260	originals are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/` and its privacy-export records.
261	The round4 findings prompted a deterministic reaction-clock test, complete
262	PowerShell analyzer coverage, corrected current-scope documentation and per-run
263	test metadata. Those changes require fresh tests and independent review; the
264	earlier chronology and unresolved reviewer-effort and prior-triage uncertainties
265	remain historical facts.

`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
and independent review justify a separate status update.

- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.

`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.

Ordered actions and expected observations:

1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.

Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.

The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).

```gherkin
Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
  Then no administrator profile is returned
  And no private catalog records are read
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
  Then the callback creates no administrator session
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
  When the administrator signs out
  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
  And the guest session remains usable
```

## Verification, operations and open dependencies

Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. The hostile-review correction adds forward
migration `012_guest_public_profiles.sql`; no package is added. Existing schema
and private Realtime/scheduler remain separate deployment prerequisites.

Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.

The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.

Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.

## Hostile-review recovery slice

Claude Opus round1 rejected candidate437c501 at92%accuracy/88%completeness.
Its full findings and persistence proof are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/`.
The owner was created with the former member public-default, without a public
preferences route. The earlier PostgreSQL public-read failure exposed the extra
row; fixture cleanup made the suite independent but did not repair that product
privacy problem. That distinction was missing from the original failure analysis.

The operator confirmed: "Hide all old member profiles". GA-10 therefore requires
new members to default private and all member identities, including retired
OpenAI records, to be excluded by the server's public query even if their stored
flag remains true. Preserve historical records, guest opt-in, ranking, paging and
revision conflicts. Add a forward SQL migration after the existing hosted history;
apply it to staging first, verify, then production. No data deletion or provider
token import is needed. Existing cached public pages may expire over their normal
five-minute read lifetime; restart/deployment creates fresh application caches.

Before this correction, the independent GA-10 oracle accepted a private member
and guest-only rows, and rejected a public member and both owner/legacy leaks.
The mock gate passed3/3 at20:22:38 on28October2026. The same oracle is bound to
the real identity service and PostgreSQL query. This is evidence for the recovery
slice, not a reconstruction of the missing original pre-implementation gate.
The original slice's chronological process receipt remains missing and is not
claimed satisfied. On28October2026 the operator explicitly answered "Record the
one-time exception" to question `call_30e2a1f3011842979ab422d87f21432e`. This is a
one-time exception for that historical missing receipt only. It does not waive
fresh hostile validation, current tests, security checks, migration verification
or hosted observations. No original chronology is reconstructed. The decision
and QBrain readback are retained in `docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/process-exception.json`.
All current status/criteria remain in progress/unsatisfied.

Recovery work also supplies explicit GA-05/06/07 cross-references to canonical
PWA criteria and their TEST/TR records, GA-09 on the responsive TR/admin TEST,
reproducible adapter fixtures and full post-edit PWA browser execution. No prior
failed review or test receipt is removed. Fresh review follows the full applicable
unit, PostgreSQL, browser, lint and production-build checks.

Claude Opus round2 rejected the corrective candidate at95%accuracy and
94%completeness. Its four FAILs were a missing mock-first gate for the deployment
planner edit, continued extension of a Node script tool, an incomplete candidate
source hash manifest, and missing pre-run analyzer receipts for the JUnit/TRX
adapter scripts. The full verdict and request/response receipts remain under
`docs/receipts/hv/`. Later reviews and dispositions are recorded below.

For the next review, a PowerShell schema planner and CLI replace the Node planner.
An initial planner module and five-case mock gate preceded the sixth test case;
the six-case gate preceded the final module edit, not the initial module. A later
catch-up gate added a rejecting negative control for every case. These receipts do
not change the original chronology. The mock-gate summary, real-run JUnit and adapted TRX receipts are in
`docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/planner-*`. The tracked source-manifest
generator enumerates literal Git paths, including bracketed routes, public assets
and root test/build configuration; the frozen review manifest records its path count.
The adapter analyzer receipt records parser and ScriptAnalyzer results for both
scripts before the fresh three-fixture run. These are local process receipts, not
approval to deploy. The final source manifest and all execution reports must be
regenerated against the frozen source revision that the next hostile review sees.

Round3 first ended incomplete during the MCP outage. Its later Claude Opus retry
returned DISAGREE at95% accuracy and93% completeness: 31 PASS, four FAIL and three
UNKNOWN. Round4 returned DISAGREE at96% accuracy and94% completeness: 35 PASS,
five FAIL and three UNKNOWN. The full request, response, findings and protected
originals are retained under `docs/receipts/hv/` and its privacy-export records.
The round4 findings prompted a deterministic reaction-clock test, complete
PowerShell analyzer coverage, corrected current-scope documentation and per-run
test metadata. Those changes require fresh tests and independent review; the
earlier chronology and unresolved reviewer-effort and prior-triage uncertainties
remain historical facts.

1	# Wordpairs Content Moderation Plan
2	
3	Current release override, 28 October 2026: [guest game and GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md)
4	disables public nominations, category submissions and role delegation. Existing
5	case/history and catalog moderation remain available only to the verified GitHub
6	owner sharpninja. The earlier multi-role community workflow below is retained as
7	historical design, not an active public entry point in this release.
8	
9	**Status:** Implemented in Phase 5 and extended by the reviewed administration/ACL pages on 27 October 2026
10	**Requirements baseline:** `word_association_game_requirements.md` v2.6  
11	**Implementation sequence:** `implementation_plan.md`  
12	**Current scope:** player nominations and category/pair suggestions; no public chat
13	
14	## 1. Purpose and scope
15	
16	This plan defines the workflow, data boundaries, reviewer experience, audit trail, and test coverage for user-submitted candidate answers and category/pair suggestions. It supports FR-16–FR-17 and AC-16–AC-19 and AC-47 in the requirements. Requirements v2.6 establishes nomination thresholds, moderator roles, reasoned decisions, one senior-moderator appeal, and catalog activation gates; retention and audit details are also fixed there. The new public landing page (FR-22/AC-43/AC-50) may show leaderboard labels and lobby summaries; this plan treats those as a separate public projection, not moderation data. It does not publish user submissions or introduce a public chat feature.
17	
18	There are two related but different flows:
19	
20	- **Candidate nomination:** a player who solves during the no-hint stage nominates a word for possible inclusion in a future answer pool. A candidate must meet the approved nomination threshold and pass moderation; even then it cannot be played until editors create a complete curated word-pair record.
21	- **Category and pair suggestion:** a player who has ten lifetime wins on one stable profile proposes one relationship category and exactly three pairs. Review and approval do not make those pairs playable until each record and the category background are complete and the curated catalog passes validation.
22	
23	The moderation process reviews content quality and suitability. It does not resolve the gameplay requirement questions, choose accepted-answer policy, or automatically promote content because it received votes. The curated catalog remains the only source of playable prompts, answers, hints, accepted alternatives, and background references.
24	
25	## 2. Product principles
26	
27	1. **Human decision for publication:** automation may check formatting, duplicates, and completeness, but only an authorized reviewer can approve user content for editorial use.
28	2. **Approval is not publication:** an approved nomination is only eligible for curation; an approved suggestion is only eligible for catalog preparation. Curated records need a separate editorial completion and release step.
29	3. **Explicit, consistent reasons:** every rejection, request for revision, and approval records a reason code and reviewer rationale. Apply the same policy to comparable submissions.
30	4. **Privacy by default:** do not expose nominator identities or private guesses to other players. The public game need not reveal reviewer identity or internal notes. Collect only the information needed to enforce eligibility and audit decisions.
31	5. **No paid moderation dependency:** use deterministic validation and human review. Do not make a paid language-model, moderation API, or other metered service a launch dependency. A later optional classifier would only prioritize/flag, never silently approve or reject.
32	6. **Separation of duties:** a submitter cannot approve their own submission. The authorized moderator/editor role is distinct from the ordinary player role. If one owner performs several roles in an early release, preserve the audit trail and expose that the review was self-administered.
33	7. **Decision records are durable:** retain an auditable history of threshold changes, reviews, status transitions, and catalog linkage. A moderation action must not rewrite nomination history.
34	8. **Keep live play safe and predictable:** only complete, approved content may enter a published catalog version. Nominations and suggestions never alter an active match.
35	
36	## 3. Policy boundary and content standards
37	
38	The requirements specify product outcomes. The content checklist below is operational guidance for human reviewers and does not change AC expectations; technical review interfaces and permissions are approved in Phase 0.
39	
40	### 3.1 Reviewer checklist
41	
42	| Review dimension | Approve when | Return/reject when |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| Eligibility | The submitter satisfies the approved gameplay/win rule; the record has required fields. | The submitter is ineligible, the nomination is from a hinted solve, or the submission is structurally incomplete. |
45	| Relationship | The prompt and answer form a clear, defensible relationship in the selected category; the relation is understandable without private context. | The pair is arbitrary, misleading, ambiguous, or categorized incorrectly. |
46	| Accuracy | Names, dates, titles, spelling, and claims are accurate enough for the approved content standard. Reviewer records a reference for disputed or non-obvious factual claims. | Material factual error cannot be corrected or the pair depends on an unsupported assertion. |
47	| Distinctiveness | The candidate adds useful variety and is not an accidental normalized duplicate of an existing candidate, pair, category, or alias. | It duplicates existing content without adding a useful accepted alternative. |
48	| Playability | The answer has a clear accepted-answer policy; three useful ordered hints can be written without revealing the answer too early; the prompt is solvable at the intended difficulty. | No fair prompt/hint sequence can be created or a hint leaks the target before its stage. |
49	| Audience and harm | Content meets the general-audience suitability baseline in the v2.6 requirements. Reviewers can flag slurs, targeted abuse, threats, personal data, sexual content, or other sensitive content for restricted review. | It violates the approved safety policy or targets a private person with abusive content. |
50	| Rights and attribution | Text/artwork can be used with appropriate permissions/notices and the pair does not depend on copying protected material beyond an approved use. | Required permission is absent, attribution is impossible, or a proposed asset conflicts with GPL distribution requirements. |
51	| Category quality | The category name is distinct, describable, and supports a coherent set of pairs and a suitable background. | It is a duplicate, too broad to guide content, or cannot be represented safely and consistently. |
52	
53	### 3.2 Resolved moderation policy
54	
55	Requirements v2.6 fixes the policy: ten unique profiles trigger review; each profile may nominate a candidate once and submit at most one candidate per eligible no-hint solve; an independent Content Moderator approves or rejects with a reason; one appeal may be submitted to a Senior Moderator; ten lifetime wins unlock one open category suggestion containing exactly three pairs. Approval does not publish incomplete content. The implementation follows the approved Phase 0 role checks, versioned state transitions and same-transaction audit contract, with separate PostgreSQL evidence for database guarantees.
56	
57	Candidate matching uses the requirements' Unicode NFKC, trim, internal-whitespace collapse and case-insensitive normalization while preserving punctuation. The submitted spelling is retained separately for reviewer display. Public aliases and leaderboard opt-out follow FR-22. Rejected or pending user content is not public or playable. The requirements' retention schedule governs audit, idempotency and outbox records; no raw incorrect guesses are persisted.
58	
59	## 4. Roles and permissions
60	
61	The 27 October 2026 [admin/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) makes the roles operational. Its permission matrix supersedes the earlier proposed separation between moderator and content-editor accounts below: moderators and senior moderators can curate approved cases and author/edit catalog pairs; administrators additionally manage role grants and revocations. Direct editorial saves require a reason and create immutable versions. Community case review and independent appeals remain mandatory for the community workflow. The admin role does not waive proposer/original-reviewer independence.
62	
63	Bootstrap administrators are defined by the server-only `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` allowlist. Other privileges are persisted in PostgreSQL, audited and checked on the server. Configured administrator authority cannot be removed through the UI, and concurrent changes cannot remove every effective administrator. There is no public privilege-escalation or role-bootstrap endpoint.
64	
65	| Role | Allowed actions | Not allowed |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| Player / submitter | Submit an eligible nomination; submit an unlocked category/pair proposal; view own submission status and public decision reason; submit one appeal to a Senior Moderator. | See another player's private nomination identity, internal reviewer notes, or unresolved drafts; approve own content; edit the live catalog. |
68	| Moderator | Review eligible cases; approve or reject with a reason; curate complete approved proposals; author/edit word pairs and hints as immutable versions; exclude content from future rounds; inspect content history. | Change vote history or scores, approve own submission, resolve appeals, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
69	| Senior moderator | All moderator permissions plus independent reasoned appeal resolution. | Resolve an appeal of own submission or original decision, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
70	| Administrator | All senior-moderator permissions plus audited role grants/revocations and user-directory access. | Bypass proposer/original-reviewer independence, remove configured administrator authority through the UI, remove the final effective administrator, or erase audit history. |

The implementation follows the approved Phase 0 role checks, versioned state transitions and same-transaction audit contract, with separate PostgreSQL evidence for database guarantees.

Candidate matching uses the requirements' Unicode NFKC, trim, internal-whitespace collapse and case-insensitive normalization while preserving punctuation. The submitted spelling is retained separately for reviewer display. Public aliases and leaderboard opt-out follow FR-22. Rejected or pending user content is not public or playable. The requirements' retention schedule governs audit, idempotency and outbox records; no raw incorrect guesses are persisted.

## 4. Roles and permissions

The 27 October 2026 [admin/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) makes the roles operational. Its permission matrix supersedes the earlier proposed separation between moderator and content-editor accounts below: moderators and senior moderators can curate approved cases and author/edit catalog pairs; administrators additionally manage role grants and revocations. Direct editorial saves require a reason and create immutable versions. Community case review and independent appeals remain mandatory for the community workflow. The admin role does not waive proposer/original-reviewer independence.

Bootstrap administrators are defined by the server-only `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` allowlist. Other privileges are persisted in PostgreSQL, audited and checked on the server. Configured administrator authority cannot be removed through the UI, and concurrent changes cannot remove every effective administrator. There is no public privilege-escalation or role-bootstrap endpoint.

| Role | Allowed actions | Not allowed |
|---|---|---|
| Player / submitter | Submit an eligible nomination; submit an unlocked category/pair proposal; view own submission status and public decision reason; submit one appeal to a Senior Moderator. | See another player's private nomination identity, internal reviewer notes, or unresolved drafts; approve own content; edit the live catalog. |
| Moderator | Review eligible cases; approve or reject with a reason; curate complete approved proposals; author/edit word pairs and hints as immutable versions; exclude content from future rounds; inspect content history. | Change vote history or scores, approve own submission, resolve appeals, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
| Senior moderator | All moderator permissions plus independent reasoned appeal resolution. | Resolve an appeal of own submission or original decision, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
| Administrator | All senior-moderator permissions plus audited role grants/revocations and user-directory access. | Bypass proposer/original-reviewer independence, remove configured administrator authority through the UI, remove the final effective administrator, or erase audit history. |

Supabase security advice includes seven private trigger/invoker functions with
mutable search paths; this is recorded rather than represented as a clean
advisory report. Existing fixed-path privileged RPCs and revoked public execution
remain in place. Provider prize-contest eligibility, physical-phone PWA checks and
formal release packaging retain their separate qualifications above.

## Current guest/admin PWA rollout in progress

The operator replaced public OpenAI sign-in and public installation with guest-only
play plus a fixed-owner GitHub admin PWA. The registered private GitHub App has
both exact hosting callbacks and no repository/organization/email/webhook access.
Server-only client configuration is present in both Vercel projects; credential
values are private. Source and QBrain changes are described in
[the current release record](admin_pwa_release.md). Existing staging evidence above
belongs to8e2f624, not the later guest/admin PWA candidate. Production remains prepared but
not deployed. No live owner sign-in, standalone phone continuity or changed-source
hosted rollout is claimed yet. All rejected build/test/HV rounds are retained.

6	    title: Lobby discovery and matching
7	    description: Players can browse discoverable open lobbies or use quick match to join an available lobby for this game. Any player in a room can share its room code or deep link to invite others; a deep link bypasses lobby browsing. Joining as a player requires an available slot under the configured capacity. An invited player who reaches a full room can choose observer mode. Before the game start countdown begins, if a player leaves a full room, the oldest observer is promoted into the final player position and the remaining players move up to close the vacancy. If player/observer membership or readiness has not changed for 30 seconds before countdown, all players are prompted once for that room version to mark ready; any such change resets the interval. When all but one player have marked ready, the holdout receives a five-second warning. If they mark ready before it expires, the countdown begins immediately. If the warning expires while the holdout remains unready in a room with more than two players, they are removed and the countdown begins. In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

In an exactly two-player lobby, the holdout remains and the lobby waits without starting the countdown until both players are ready. The roster locks when the countdown begins, and a player who leaves afterward is not replaced. Rooms are private by default; the creator may enable discoverability. Quick match selects the oldest eligible room, breaking equal creation times by stable room ID. These joins use the same atomic capacity check.

# Functional Requirements (MCP Server)

## FR-ACCESSCONTROL-024 Moderator and administrator access control

Allow authorized administrators to grant and revoke moderator, senior-moderator and administrator rights; bootstrap explicit existing profile IDs from server configuration.
Scope: layer-1+
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS is a private server-only comma-separated allowlist of stable existing profile IDs. Empty configuration grants no bootstrap authority and aliases/browser input cannot grant access. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)
- [x] Moderators moderate and curate; senior moderators additionally resolve independent appeals; administrators additionally manage users. Proposer/original-reviewer independence remains enforced. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)
- [x] Roles are read from trusted current server/database evidence; configured administrator authority cannot be revoked in the UI and the final effective administrator cannot be removed, including concurrent cross-revocation. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)
- [x] Role changes atomically persist revision, canonical retry result and reasoned audit. Revoked administrators cannot replay old grants to regain authority; directories omit credentials, emails and OIDC subjects. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)

## FR-ADMINPAGES-023 Administration pages

Provide owner-only GitHub administration at /admin and /admin/words; public guest play and inactive role grants cannot authorize access. Keep immutable, audited content commands and safe retries.
Scope: layer-1+
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Authorized staff can search/filter the moderation queue at /admin, approve/reject with reasons, review history and independently resolve permitted appeals. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)
- [ ] /admin/words supports audited immutable word/hint editing. User delegation is disabled: /admin/users redirects to /admin and its API returns404 without reading/writing access storage. (evidence: Unverified changed-release obligation; prior evidence retained in notes. Specification: docs/admin_pwa_release.md.)
- [x] Ordinary players cannot fetch privileged records or perform administrative writes; stale authorized GET responses cannot restore private data after an authorization denial. (evidence: docs/admin_acl_design.md; docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json; tests/browser/admin.phase6.spec.ts; tests/integration/admin.integration.ts)

docs/phase2_execution.md:22:The disposable runner uses pinned Postgres and Supabase Realtime images, random loopback ports and owned container IDs. It installs the Realtime fixture's actual role/schema prerequisites and waits for both tenant tables and the HTTP service; seed tables alone do not establish readiness. It removes only containers it created. Local fixture credentials are never live account credentials.
docs/admin_acl_design.md:89:Tab-local drafts, verified session generations, native profile Save/Cancel/Escape, canonical uncertain-command retention and acknowledged success results now survive authorized in-tab navigation. Authorization denial invalidates older reads before private data can return. The existing live room transport remains separately verified; fixture browser UI evidence does not establish the full real private-push player-count matrix.

This temporary leased runtime preserves the game database and is not a Vercel/Supabase cloud deployment. A cloud deployment must provide an independent deadline/outbox trigger and verify actual private delivery before release; browser polling does not establish scheduler health.

# Round 5 review of 6071b2d: DISAGREE, accuracy 97, completeness 95

Both scores are below 98, so this revision is not ready for staging. The three failures are all low severity, but there are still three failures and four open unknowns.

- **Revision:** 6071b2d6750b875864ce11011f1aff26243f29e6, compared against 8e2f624.
- **Reviewer:** model claude-opus-5-5, confirmed by this runtime. Effort is "high" according to the launch command only; nothing inside the session confirms it.
- **Session:** `ClaudeCode-20261029T144329Z-plugin-session`, request `req-20261029T144333Z-prompt-73ea`. It is linked to parent `Codex-20261027T100516Z-plugin-session` / `req-20261029T135928Z-prompt-c0e1` and earlier retry `req-20261029T042903Z-prompt-c233`.
- **Verdict file:** `docs/receipts/hv/20261029T094325-admin-pwa-source-round5.verdict.json` (sha256 3DB0A843). It holds all 44 items, 12 findings and the session readback.
- **Counts:** 37 PASS, 3 FAIL, 4 UNKNOWN, out of 44 items.

## Failures

1. **S1-08 / F-R5-1: the reaction failures are kept but never analyzed.**
   - Round 4 asked for the original failure's error-context file and a written cause analysis. Neither exists, and no reason was recorded for dropping them.
   - The three failed clock experiments are kept:
     - v1 failed 3 of 3: the button was still disabled after the 1 ms step.
     - v2 failed 3 of 3: the button was already enabled at 1999 ms.
     - v3 failed 1 of 3 with "Cannot fast-forward to the past".
   - Their receipts have no command, host or run ID, and their error-context attachments point into the temporary `test-results/` folder.
   - No document says the original round-4 failure is still unexplained.
   - This repeats a round-3 finding (I-R3-7: kept failures not analyzed).
   - Fix: write up each experiment (what changed, what happened, any labeled guess at the cause), keep the error-context files, and add command, host and run ID to each experiment receipt.
2. **S1-12 / F-R5-2: the planner run records don't give exact commands.**
   - The unit, PostgreSQL and browser runs now record run ID b79af43e, host, revision, timing, full command and exit code. That part is fixed.
   - The planner records are not exact:
     - The planner-real and negative-control records give a script path with no executable and no exit code.
     - The planner-mock record paraphrases its Pester configuration instead of giving a runnable command.
     - The `WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE` setting sits outside the command.
     - No committed script produces `mock.xml`, so that run can't be reproduced from the record.
   - The three script-contract runs have no JUnit or TRX files and are not in the evidence index.
   - Fix: commit the script that produced the planner evidence, record executable, arguments, module setting and exit code for each run, and add JUnit/TRX plus index entries for the contract runs.
3. **S4-02 / F-R5-3: the same stale-text problem remains in other documents.**
   - Only the two `deployment_plan.md` lines named in round 4 were fixed. These still describe the old scope as current:
     - `moderation_plan.md:63` and `:70` (admin bootstrap from `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS`, admins managing role grants)
     - `implementation_plan.md:20` (public home-screen install)
     - `hosting_execution.md:162-166` (OpenAI sign-in as a pending dependency)
     - `local_development.md:25,39,41` (bootstrap setup and grants at `/admin/users`)
   - The same text went out in the wiki export.
   - The docs check round 4 proposed was not added.
   - Fix: mark these lines historical or replace them with a reference to `admin_pwa_release.md`, and add the docs check.

## Unknowns

- **S1-19:** my effort level isn't confirmed inside the session.
- **S1-20:** what happened to the earlier triage failsafe report (`...5ca5`) still can't be checked.
- **S2-07:** there's no artifact showing the Copy Invitation Link change was planned and approved before it was implemented.
- **S1-21:** the remote wiki state is unchecked. `wiki-publication.json` says it was published at facb58bb, but `wiki-export.json` still says publication is pending, and my web fetch was denied.

## Passes

- **Evidence:** all ten JUnit/TRX hashes match. Unit 588, PostgreSQL 68, browser 78 and planner 6/6 (mock and real) all pass with 0 failed and 0 skipped, and test names pair one to one. All of it ran after the commit. The 279-path source manifest matches the committed tree byte for byte, and the product source hasn't changed since round 4.
- **Round-4 fixes:**
  - F-R4-2 is fixed. All 22 repository PowerShell files are clean, their hashes match 6071b2d, my own analyzer run agrees, and all 10 suppressions carry written justifications.
  - F-R4-3 is fixed. The planner timeline in `admin_pwa_release.md` now matches the receipts.
  - F-R4-5 is fixed for the two named lines.
  - The reaction test itself is now sound. The browser clocks are paused and advance together, a component test pins 1999 ms (disabled) and 2000 ms (enabled), it passed 25 repeats, and it passed in the full suite.
- **QBrain:**
  - FR-LOBBYDISCOVERY-019 and TEST-ROOMINVITATIONS-025 carry INVITE-COPY-01/02/03; TR-SCHEMA-PROVISIONING-023 and TEST-SCHEMAPROVISIONING-123 carry TR-23-C02.
  - All four records are in progress with those criteria not yet satisfied.
  - All four are linked from FR-019's 71 native links, and the criterion texts appear in the requirements export.
  - FR-ACCESSCONTROL-024 is correctly marked deferred.
- **Not claimed:** nothing is claimed done or deployed. Hosted OAuth consent, physical install, migration 012 on staging and production, and production itself are all still pending. No credential appears in any tracked file or public copy (0 full-key matches in 1,172 files).

The JSON has the full PASS item list: S1-01 to S1-07, S1-09 to S1-11, S1-13 to S1-18, S2-01 to S2-06, S2-08 to S2-10, S3-01 to S3-08, and S4-01, S4-03 to S4-05. It also has 9 informational findings. The one most likely to matter: the browser reaction test sees the display only every 250 ms, so the exact 2-second boundary is pinned by the component test alone.

## Session proof and my own errors

- **Turn readback (10:06:21):** status completed, 67 dialog items, 8 actions (6 of them design decisions), 44 item lines, 12 finding objects, verdict JSON in 9 parts, and the verdict text in the response. The history query shows the parent and earlier-retry tags.
- **Wrong model field:** the history record lists this Claude session's model as "codex". Round 4 already filed this under triage report 8ae42634; I did not file it again.
- **My mistake:** I first told you Bash was fully denied. It wasn't: only my plain directory listing was blocked, and `pwsh -File` is allowed. I corrected that and it's recorded in the turn.
- **Rewritten draft:** my first verdict-builder script had two analyzer warnings, so I rewrote it before running it.

I made no product, requirement, TODO or Git changes, and ran no builds, tests or browsers. I wrote only the git-ignored tools folder, the session turn and the verdict file.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The failed clock experiments point to a likely mechanism, but only as an inference. The room screen recalibrates its display clock from the server time on every refetch. If the test fixture's time jumps ahead before the browser's paused clock catches up, the display skews. That's why the final test moves both clocks forward in matching steps of 250 ms or less.
- Repeating a test 25 times shows it's stable now; it doesn't explain why it failed before. That's why the missing write-up is a separate failure from the test fix.
- Round-4 findings often repeated a problem across several documents, and fixing only the named lines leaves the rest. A sweep for every instance plus an automated docs check catches them all.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
